Custom logo drinkware: MOQs, print methods and an artwork checklist

What drives the minimum order on a decorated item, which print method to specify, and exactly what to send us so the proof matches the production run.

What actually sets the minimum order

The MOQ on a decorated order is not arbitrary. It is driven by three things: the setup cost of the decoration process, the print position, and the risk of a colour mismatch across a run. Setup is a fixed cost — the screen or pad tooling, the machine time to dial in registration, and the first-off approval. Spread across 200 pieces it is unaffordable; spread across 5,000 it disappears.

In practice the minimum is set by the process and by the print area rather than by a single house number. Multi-colour work and full-wrap artwork rise from there because each colour adds a setup and a registration step. Laser engraving has a higher setup but needs no ink and no drying, which can make it competitive on longer runs.

For small bar tools — pourers, stoppers, sippers — the print area is small enough that minimums can be lower than for drinkware. It is worth asking, because a campaign can be built across two budget lines by quoting the small bar tool and the glassware in the same request.

Choosing between the print methods

The most common mistake is choosing pad printing for an item that will be washed in a commercial dishwasher for three years. If the buyer's environment is hospitality, laser engraving is usually the right answer even though the unit cost is higher.

  • Pad printing — one or two colours, fine detail on curved surfaces, lowest unit cost. The default choice for corporate and event programmes.
  • Silk screen — larger and flatter print areas, heavier ink coverage, good for a bold single-colour mark.
  • Laser engraving — the mark is cut into the surface, so it cannot wear off. Choose this where the item will be washed repeatedly or gifted as a keepsake.
  • Electroplating with a logo — a metallic or mirror finish with the mark integrated into the finish. Used on premium bar tools and novelty drinkware.
  • Moulded-in logo — the mark is part of the tool itself. The most durable option, and realistic on high-volume shapes where the tooling cost can be amortised.

The artwork checklist

The last item on that list changes the packaging answer. A corporate giveaway needs a plain export carton; a retail shelf needs a printed colour box, a hang tag and a UPC barcode. Telling us the channel at quotation stage means packaging is priced into the unit cost instead of appearing as a surprise later.

  • Vector format: AI, EPS or PDF. Bitmap files must be redrawn, which adds cost and time.
  • Pantone reference for every colour, plus a reference for any colour match on the product itself
  • The exact print position and maximum print dimensions
  • Text converted to outlines so there is no font substitution
  • Any trademark or licensed mark, with confirmation that the buyer holds the rights
  • The channel the product is going into — corporate giveaway, retail shelf, or e-commerce listing

Approval gates: proof, sample, then production

Every decorated programme runs through two gates. First a virtual proof, where you check layout, scale and colour against your artwork. Second, where the finish is colour-sensitive, a physical pre-production sample for sign-off. Nothing enters bulk production until you approve in writing.

This is what stops the classic failure mode of branded orders: a client approving a description of a colour rather than a physical item, then rejecting the shipment because the shade is not what they imagined. A colour chip costs a fraction of a rejected container.

Questions on this topic

What is the minimum order for logo printing?

The minimum for each decoration method is confirmed per SKU and per decoration method in the quotation.

Is laser engraving better than printing?

Laser engraving is more durable because the mark is cut into the material rather than applied to the surface. Pad printing is cheaper per unit for short runs. For hospitality items that will be washed repeatedly, engraving is usually the right choice.

What file format do you need for artwork?

Vector artwork in AI, EPS or PDF, with text converted to outlines. Send bitmap files if that is all you have and we will confirm whether they can be redrawn and what that costs.

Can you print our logo in a specific Pantone colour?

Yes. Send the Pantone reference and we will produce a colour chip or moulded sample for approval before production starts.

Why does each SKU have its own MOQ?

MOQ is maintained at SKU/model level because it follows the mould, the material and the decoration route for that exact model. It is never calculated from a category name, so two similar-looking items can carry different minimums.

How MOQ works

Why do the standard order, the decorated order and the gift-box build have different MOQs?

The blank bulk order, the logo decoration and the custom gift-box build are three different production routes. Each one has its own setup and its own minimum for the same model, so a single figure would be misleading.

Gift box packaging guide

Which order inputs determine the final MOQ?

The SKU, the quantity, the decoration method, the decoration area, the packaging configuration and the destination. Change any one of them and the confirmed minimum can change with it.

Request a quote

When should a buyer choose a standard SKU instead of a new packaging configuration?

Choose the standard configuration when the requirement is the item itself. Choose a new packaging configuration when the retail or gift presentation is part of what you are selling, because that route carries its own setup and minimum.

Gift box packaging guide

What should a buyer prepare before asking for a custom quote?

The SKU or product link, the quantity, the logo file, the decoration and packaging requirement, the destination country and the target delivery date. With those inputs the MOQ, the production route and the freight basis are all confirmed in one quotation.

Request a quote

How should a distributor plan the first order quantity?

Plan the first quantity from the confirmed MOQ for the exact configuration and the sell-through you expect on that model, then hold the balance of the range for the reorder. Send the model list and the expected volumes so the quantities are quoted together.
